title: CORREL and PEARSON use population normalisation (n) with stored-PC64 two-pass arithmetic, while RSQ squares the sample-normalised (n-1) correlation
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527 (dc-wli1), CORREL and PEARSON divide centred sums of squares and cross-products by n (population variance/covariance) using x87 64-bit intermediate additions/products stored to binary64 at each step in the first-pass means, second-pass centred sums, roots, and final division. By contrast, RSQ squares the sample-normalised (n-1) correlation in binary64, so mathematically equivalent three-point inputs produce distinct last bits in RSQ (0x3fdb6db6db6db6da vs 0x3fdb6db6db6db6dd) while CORREL and PEARSON match 0x3fe4f2ec413cb52b.
basis: Measured across 414 identification/holdout vectors, 92 accumulation controls, 47 precision holdout vectors, and 438 corpus CORREL cells in Excel 16.0.20527 (docs/research/correlation-arithmetic-2026-11-12.md), plus 2,853/2,853 CORREL, 2,854/2,854 PEARSON, and 2,852/2,852 RSQ full-bank rows.
inferred: That the stored-PC64 operation graph holds for all vector lengths beyond the mined holdout controls (with integer division by n indistinguishable on small counts) is inferred from dc-wli1; the raw probe JSONs were archived to R2 rather than committed.
